description: We're a group of Northwestern Engineers who want to make an interdisciplinary project!
summary: Wake Up, Oppy is an interactive educational experience about NASA’s Opportunity rover. It helps players understand how the rover works by letting them assemble its major systems, inspect them in 3D, and then explore the rover’s mission on Mars by following an interactive timeline with mission events, Mars imagery, and a route map. The site also includes ambient audio, interaction sounds, and a rotatable, zoomable 3D model of Oppy. Together, these features connect the rover’s physical design to the work it did on Mars. The project is designed to work as a browser-based activity or as a hands-on exhibit with NFC hardware, making the same rover story accessible with or without a physical setup. This project aims to inspire curiosity of space exploration and technology in both school-age and casual space enthusiasts alike, hoping to inspire the next generation of scientists and engineers.
details:
"Wake Up, Oppy!" is an interactive, educational experience that introduces users to NASA’s Opportunity rover (Oppy) by letting users “rebuild” a 3D model of Oppy one part at a time using on-screen or NFC-tagged miniature parts, then explore the rovers system and mission.

How it works:

In the physical world, users pick up a miniature part of Oppy, scan it on the base, and the webpage will register that part. Based on what the software registers, that rover part will appear on the page with its information. Once the solar array, instrument arm, camera mast, and wheels are assembled, players wake Opportunity and explore key moments from her journey. The site includes a Hardware mode that connects to a compatible RFID/NFC reader to scan the parts, as well as a Browser mode as a standalone for interacting without hardware. 

What we hope to achieve:

We hope Wake Up, Oppy makes rover engineering and Mars exploration approachable through hands-on play. By connecting physical parts to an interactive 3D rover and mission story, players will be able to connect each part and its contributions to space exploration. This interactive web-based demo is meant to foster curiosity for all young space enjoyers and classrooms -- even if they don't have the open-sourced 3D-Printed hardware!

Main Considerations:

  • We wanted our tool to make NASA hardware more "hands-on" -- literally! Many of our parts can be manipulated and positioned. All 3D model files are open-source and can be downloaded & printed on most entry-level 3D printers.
  • We wanted our tool to be usable without the hardware we demonstrate. Therefore, Oppy can be built without a scanning plate by using the keyboard.

Tools, development, and hardware:

  • HTML, CSS, JavaScript, with Three.js for the 3D rover
  • Web Serial connects supported RFID hardware
  • Teensy 4.1, Platform IO, C & C++ (for programming the scanning platform)
  • 3D Printed Parts (for Opportunity’s Mechanisms)
  • OnShape (for designing all 3D Printed Hardware)
  • Bambu Labs A1, Bambu Slicer, Prusa Slicer

Use of Super Intelligence (SI):

  • Claude and ChatGPT for code generation, debugging, and optimization
  • Claude for fetching additional helpful resources during the research phase.
